title: Output stewardship, sidecar shims and compatibility notes
body:
Purpose:

This is a working note for how we manage Terraform module outputs across private deployment primitives (VPC, IAM, EKS/GKE/AKS) with a focus on backward compatibility and safe upgrade paths for customers in VPC/on-prem environments. The goal is pragmatic: allow module authors to evolve interfaces while providing predictable migration and rollback patterns for consumers (internal and customers).

Scope:
- Terraform primitive modules: vpc, iam, cluster (eks/gke/aks), networking addons
- Outputs and variables that are widely consumed across stacks: subnets, route_table_ids, bastion_ips, kubeconfig outputs, service_account_arns, iam_role_arns, cloud-specific cluster ids
- On-prem and VPC differences (e.g., no cloud-managed cluster id on air-gapped installs)

Design principles:
1) Output stability over brevity: once an output is published, maintain it (name + type + semantic meaning) for at least one major release cycle.
2) Non-breaking expansion only: add new outputs rather than change existing ones. When renaming is necessary, add a shim (deprecated name) that forwards to the new output for >= 2 releases.
3) Explicit deprecation metadata: outputs that are being retired must have an explicit deprecation note in docs + automated plan-time warnings.
4) Guard rails: automated tests (plan-only) that detect when an output type changes or is removed. Fail CI on unexpected breaking changes unless flagged with an approved RFC.

Pattern: Sidecar shim outputs
Motivation: many downstream stacks read module outputs by name. Changing an output name or type causes immediate breakages. The sidecar shim pattern gives module authors a low-risk path to evolve outputs without immediate consumer changes.

How it works (high level):
- Module exposes canonical outputs (principal names)
- Module also exposes a short-lived shim output with the old name that simply references the canonical value and sets a deprecation notice in README
- CI enforces that shims include a 'deprecation_version' and an automated deprecation-reminder in our CHANGELOG pipeline

Example: renaming 'kube_admin_config' -> 'kubeconfig_admin':
- Add new output: kubeconfig_admin = module.cluster.kubeconfig_admin
- Keep old: kube_admin_config = module.cluster.kubeconfig_admin # DEPRECATED: removed in vX.Y
- Add README snippet and deprecation_version = "vX.Y" metadata comment

Concrete Terraform excerpt (for module outputs.tf):

# canonical output
output "kubeconfig_admin" {
  value = local.kubeconfig_admin
  description = "Admin kubeconfig (base64) for the cluster. canonical."
}

# shim for backwards compatibility
output "kube_admin_config" {
  value = local.kubeconfig_admin
  description = "DEPRECATED: use kubeconfig_admin. Will be removed in vX.Y."
}

Compatibility matrix suggestion:
- Columns: module, output_name, type, first_published_version, deprecated_in_version, removed_in_version, consumers (teams/repos), notes
- Maintain as a CSV in repo root and render to Confluence for quick reference

Migration and upgrade playbook (consumer-facing):
1) Identify outputs used by your stack: terraform state pull -> parse outputs or run `terraform output -json` on each env.
2) Cross-check against compatibility matrix; identify shims and deprecated outputs.
3) Prioritize: if only shims used -> plan replacement and test in a non-prod workspace.
4) For outputs that change type (string -> list), add an adapter in your code: `tolist()` / `join()` as appropriate and run full plan to confirm no diff.
5) Run smoke deploy and integration tests that exercise any core module outputs (esp. kubeconfig, IAM ARNs, subnet IDs).
6) Rollout: use workspace-per-env + canary environment to validate before rolling to prod workspaces.

Automated validation and CI hooks:
- Pre-merge check in module repo: run `tfsec`/`terraform validate` and a custom script that compares outputs in this PR against latest published module release's outputs.json (CI artifact). If key/type removed -> fail unless PR includes approved "output-removal" label with RFC link.
- Consumer repo CI: plan-time warnings when it detects use of outputs with 'DEPRECATED' in description. Provide actionable message: which module release removes it and replacement.

Versioning and release policy:
- Module MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH semantics. Breaking changes (removals, type changes) require MAJOR bump.
- We prefer additive MINOR releases for new outputs. Shims live for at least 2 minor releases.
- Release checklist must include updating the compatibility CSV and publishing a release note with exact removal timeline.

Edge cases specific to on-prem:
- Missing cloud-managed fields: some outputs (e.g., cloud_cluster_id) may not exist. Modules must provide consistent null/empty values and document the semantics. Prefer explicit `null` output instead of omission so consumers can unify checks.
- Secrets handling: outputs that contain secrets (kubeconfigs, ARNs with keys) must be marked in description and not included in public artifact snapshots. Use `sensitive = true` where appropriate.

Testing matrix (must be automated in PR):
- Unit: terraform validate + fmt + simple plan using a minimal example consumer
- Integration: full plan for dev workspace (canary) with `TF_LOG=TRACE` capture for memory of differences
- Contract tests: a small python/golang script that loads previous outputs.json (published as release artifact) and asserts all previously published outputs still exist and have compatible types (or that a shim exists).

Operational runbooks (upgrade/remediation):
- If a downstream break occurs after module upgrade:
  1) Pin module to last working tag in the consumer (terraform init -upgrade? -> replace with version constraint), run `terraform apply` to revert state if needed.
  2) Open hotfix PR in module to reintroduce shim output if removal was accidental.
  3) Coordinate with impacted teams via Slack #priv-deploy-alerts and create a short-lived branch in consumer repos to adapt to new output.

Checklist for module authors before merging output changes:
- [ ] Update compatibility CSV
- [ ] Add shim with DEPRECATED description if renaming
- [ ] Mark sensitive outputs as `sensitive = true`
- [ ] Add plan-time tests to PR CI
- [ ] Document deprecation in README with removal version
- [ ] Notify mailing list: infra-announce@redwood.ai

Open questions / discussion points:
- How strict should we be about types? Example: an output was string historically but effectively contained comma-separated values. Do we normalize to list on new output and leave shim as string? (proposed: allow type change only if shim preserves the old type but new output gets canonical typed value)
- How long is too long for a shim to live? Suggested policy: max 12 months or 2 minor releases, whichever is longer; require explicit extension approval after that.
- Cross-cloud name collisions: when a module supports multiple clouds, should outputs be cloud-prefixed (aws_subnet_ids vs subnet_ids)? Propose canonical names (cloud-agnostic) with cloud-specific additional outputs when required.

Next steps / action items:
- (Aisha) Draft a PR for infra repo to add the compatibility CSV as a release artifact (due 2025-02-09).
- (Marco) Prototype CI contract test script and add to module template (due 2025-01-24).
- (Evelyn) Run audit across top 20 customer stacks to identify highest-risk outputs (due 2025-02-02).

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally pragmatic and aims to reduce customer outages caused by module churn. The sidecar shim pattern trades a small amount of API clutter for significantly lower upgrade risk. If the team prefers, we can pilot this pattern on a small set of modules (vpc + cluster) for 3 months and iterate.

References and helpful links:
- TF module guidelines: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/TF+Module+Standards
- Example PR where we added a shim: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1892
- Upgrade incident post-mortem (internal): JIRA-PRIVDEPLOY-412
